topic: Dumb Gateways Turn Slow Microservices into Total Outages
postText:
In healthcare IT, a slow reporting service once drained our API gateway worker pools. Because routes shared one connection pool, critical triage systems stalled alongside routine report queries.

Here is the hard truth: when one downstream service crawls, an unprotected API gateway amplifies the failure instead of containing it.

Here is how we stopped cascading outages at our gateway:

1. Bulkhead Connection Pools
Never allow all routes to draw from a shared thread or connection pool. Allocate discrete, bounded pools per upstream domain. If billing or analytics stalls, critical patient registration keeps humming.

2. Distributed Token-Bucket Throttling
Global IP rate limits are not enough. Rate limit by upstream route sensitivity. When downstream latency spikes, dynamically tighten ingress token generation to preserve backend headroom.

3. Fast-Failing Circuit Breakers with Fallbacks
Trip circuits on p99 latency breaches, not just 5xx errors. When tripped, fail fast with an explicit HTTP 503 or return a cached read-model fallback. Holding gateway sockets open waiting on 30-second timeouts kills your cluster.

How do you balance circuit breaker trip sensitivity between critical write endpoints and heavy read queries?
